title: Pacing and cut rhythm
purpose: Measures shot lengths, cut rate, acceleration, holds and how cuts line up with speech and music, then states them as pacing rules.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F11 scene scores to find dissolves and false cuts; F1 frames either side of doubtful cuts.
pitfalls: Trusting a shot detector on dissolves, flashes or fast pans
Calling cuts on-beat when tempo detection failed or the tolerance is wider than half a beat
Ignoring the hook when describing overall pacing

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.number: {"value": n, "unit": "..."} optionally with "min" and "max"; becomes an IR observed_number
answer_types.ms: {"value": n, "unit": "ms"} optionally with "min"/"max"; signed when an offset (negative = earlier)
answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.parameter: one IR parameter object (name, type, description, default, min/max or choices, derived_from)
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F2: Burst sheet, 10 frames over 1 s: ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 1 -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=10,scale=270:-2,tile=5x2" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/burst_T.jpg"
recipes.F5: Per-frame motion in a region (mean absolute frame difference, 0-255): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "crop=iw:ih*0.15:0:0,tblend=all_mode=difference,signalstats,metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=$WORK/diff.txt" -an -f null -  (drop the crop for the full frame)
recipes.F8: Every frame in a short window (animation timing; frame k is at T + k/fps): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t 0.5 -i "$SRC" -vf "scale=540:-2" "$WORK/step_T_%03d.png"
recipes.F10: Similarity of two frames (SSIM, 1.0 = identical): ffmpeg -i a.jpg -i b.jpg -lavfi "[0:v]scale=320:-2[a];[1:v]scale=320:-2[b];[a][b]ssim" -f null - 2>&1 | grep -o "All:[0-9.]*"
recipes.F11: Per-frame scene-change score (finds dissolves and missed cuts): ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "select='gte(scene,0)',metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.scene_score:file=$WORK/scene.txt" -an -f null -
recipes.A1: Spectrogram image (add highpass=f=3000, before showspectrumpic to isolate clicks and whooshes): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -t D -i "$SRC" -lavfi "showspectrumpic=s=1200x600:legend=1" "$WORK/spec_T.png"

questions.question: What is the median shot length over the whole video?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills timeline.median_shot_s, the main pacing parameter.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.shot_stats.median_s (video_re_shot_stats); report evidence.shot_stats.count in the note.
questions.challenge: Recompute the median from evidence.shots[].duration_s; check F11 scene scores for missed dissolves which would lengthen shots.

questions.question: What is the cut rate in cuts per minute?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills timeline.cut_rate_per_min.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.shot_stats.cut_rate_per_min; equivalently (count - 1) / duration_s x 60.
questions.challenge: Recompute from count and duration; a mismatch above 5% means one of the fields is stale.

questions.question: What is the median shot length in the first 10 seconds versus the rest of the video?
questions.why_it_matters: Captures front-loaded pacing as a two-speed rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Split evidence.shots[] by start_s < 10; report both medians and their ratio.
questions.challenge: With fewer than 4 shots in the first 10 s, the first median is weak; say so.

questions.question: What is the shot-length distribution (p10, median, p90) and its coefficient of variation?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the allowed spread around the target median in the compiler.
questions.how_to_answer: Compute from evidence.shots[].duration_s.
questions.challenge: Recompute; exclude a first or last shot that is a leader or end card and report the difference.

questions.question: Do shots get shorter or longer over the course of the video (slope of shot length against time)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes an acceleration rule or confirms constant pacing.
questions.how_to_answer: Fit duration_s against start_s with least squares; report slope in seconds of shot length per minute and the first-third versus last-third medians.
questions.challenge: Check that a long end card is not driving the slope.

questions.question: What share of cuts land on a detected musical beat?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills audio.cuts_on_beat_ratio.
questions.how_to_answer: Read evidence.audio.cuts_on_beat_ratio (video_re_cut_beat_alignment); report the tolerance it used and evidence.audio.tempo_bpm.
questions.challenge: Compute the chance rate: tolerance window x 2 / beat period. A ratio near chance does not support 'cuts on beat'.

questions.question: What share of cuts fall within 150 ms of the end of a speech segment (cutting on pauses)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule to cut on speech pauses or not.
questions.how_to_answer: For each cut time (shots[].start_s, excluding 0), find the nearest speech segment end in audio.speech_segments; report the share within 150 ms.
questions.challenge: Compare with the share for randomly shifted cut times (shift all cuts by 0.7 s) to show the effect is not chance.

questions.question: What share of cuts happen in the middle of a word (speech continues across the cut)?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the editor whether picture changes are tied to words.
questions.how_to_answer: A cut is mid-speech if it falls inside a speech segment more than 100 ms from both ends; report the share.
questions.challenge: Speech segments merge short pauses; check two flagged cuts on an A1 spectrogram.

questions.question: Where is the longest shot, how long is it, and what happens during it (reveal, text-heavy explanation, end card)?
questions.why_it_matters: Shows where the format deliberately holds.
questions.how_to_answer: Max of shots[].duration_s; inspect F2 bursts across it.
evidence_required: frames: F2 across the longest shot
questions.challenge: Check with F11 that the longest shot is not two shots joined by a missed dissolve.

questions.question: Are there flash shots shorter than 0.25 s, how many, and what are they used for?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds flash accents to the effect list if deliberate.
questions.how_to_answer: Filter shots[] by duration_s < 0.25; inspect each with F8.
questions.challenge: Encoder artefacts and detector double-triggers produce fake short shots; each must be seen on F8.

questions.question: Do shot lengths alternate (long-short-long) or follow another repeating rhythm?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rhythm pattern in the generation rules.
questions.how_to_answer: Compute the lag-1 autocorrelation of shot durations; negative values suggest alternation. Also write the first 12 durations rounded to 0.1 s.
questions.challenge: Autocorrelation on fewer than 15 shots is noisy; report n and keep confidence low.

questions.question: What is the median shot length per beat role (hook, items, outro)?
questions.why_it_matters: Lets the compiler pace each beat role differently.
questions.how_to_answer: Assign each shot to a beat using the structure lens boundaries; compute medians per role.
questions.challenge: Shots straddling a boundary must be assigned by majority overlap; check the rule was applied.

questions.question: How many visual events per second occur when counting cuts plus text appearances plus distinct zoom or colour jumps?
questions.why_it_matters: Captures total visual change rate, which cut rate alone misses.
questions.how_to_answer: Merge event times: shots[].start_s, distinct text_regions t_s where a new region appears, and jumps seen on F2 bursts at 5 sampled points; divide by duration.
questions.challenge: Make sure the same event is not counted twice when a cut and a caption change coincide.

questions.question: What is the longest stretch without any visual change (no cut, no new text, no visible motion change)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a max_static_s constraint.
questions.how_to_answer: From the merged event list (013) find the largest gap; confirm with F5 full-frame difference that motion is low during it.
questions.challenge: A continuous camera move is a change; check F5 values during the gap.

questions.question: What share of caption changes coincide with a cut (within 100 ms)?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether captions and cuts are scheduled together.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare captions[].start_s with shots[].start_s.
questions.challenge: If captions come from transcription, they are not on-screen timings; use text_regions instead or lower confidence.

questions.question: Are cuts made on action (movement continues across the cut) or on stillness?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes an editing rule for motion footage.
questions.how_to_answer: Use F5 full-frame difference values in the 3 frames before each of 6 sampled cuts; high values mean on-action.
questions.challenge: Virtual zooms on stills always show motion; use not-applicable-stills for photo montages.

questions.question: How many jump cuts are there (cut between two shots with the same framing and subject)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds jump cuts as a technique for presenter-led formats.
questions.how_to_answer: F10 SSIM between the last frame of each shot and the first frame of the next; values above 0.8 with a cut indicate a jump cut.
questions.challenge: A punch-in zoom changes framing and lowers SSIM; check flagged and unflagged pairs by eye.

questions.question: On average, how many spoken phrases does one shot cover (shots per phrase)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule tying shot count to script phrases.
questions.how_to_answer: Count speech segments (or caption cards) and shots; ratio = shots / phrases.
questions.challenge: Say which unit was used for phrases; the two give different ratios.

questions.question: What is the median shot length measured in musical beats at the detected tempo?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives a tempo-relative pacing rule that transfers to new music.
questions.how_to_answer: median_s x tempo_bpm / 60.
questions.challenge: If tempo_bpm is null or the music has no clear pulse (check A1), answer 'not determinable'.

questions.question: What are the median and maximum gaps between speech segments?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets narration pause lengths in the TTS plan.
questions.how_to_answer: Compute gaps between consecutive audio.speech_segments.
questions.challenge: Check two long gaps with A4 silencedetect; music-filled gaps may be missed by VAD.

questions.question: Does pacing slow down before the payoff (longer shots or pauses in the last 25% before the reveal)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a pre-payoff hold rule.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare median shot length in the 10 s before the payoff beat with the item median.
questions.challenge: Require a change of at least 25% to call it a slow-down.

questions.question: What share of shot changes use a transition (dissolve, wipe, zoom) rather than a hard cut?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the hard-cut default and transition frequency.
questions.how_to_answer: Use F11 scene scores: hard cuts are single-frame spikes; transitions spread over several frames. Sample at least 10 boundaries with F8.
questions.challenge: Report the sample size; extrapolating from 3 boundaries is over-generalisation.

questions.question: Is the first shot of each item longer than the item's other shots (a pacing reset at item start)?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule for item-opening shots.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare first-shot duration with the median of other shots per item.
questions.challenge: Count how many items follow the pattern; under two thirds means false.

questions.question: Write the shot-count rule for a beat in terms of parameters (for example shots = ceil(beat_s / target_median_shot_s)).
questions.why_it_matters: Gives the compiler a procedural shot plan.
questions.how_to_answer: Fit the observed shots per beat against beat duration; propose the rule and report its error on each beat.
questions.challenge: Recompute shots for each observed beat from the rule; errors of more than one shot on more than a third of beats reject it.

questions.question: What range should target_median_shot_s have, justified by the spread observed in this video?
questions.why_it_matters: Turns one observation into a parameter with an evidence-based range.
questions.how_to_answer: Default = observed median; min/max = p25 and p75 of item shot lengths; derived_from = pacing_cut_rhythm-001 and -004.
questions.challenge: Any range wider than the observed p10-p90 must be marked assumed.

questions.question: Does the picture change before the new sentence starts, and by how many milliseconds (cut lead)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the cut-to-voice offset in the editing rule.
questions.how_to_answer: For cuts within 400 ms of a speech segment start, compute start_speech - cut_time; report median (positive = picture leads).
questions.challenge: Speech segment onsets can lag the true onset; check two on A1.

questions.question: What is the micro-timing inside an item start (for example cut at +0 ms, label at +150 ms, number at +400 ms, voice at +300 ms)?
questions.why_it_matters: Gives frame-accurate offsets for the per-item template.
questions.how_to_answer: F8 frame steps over the first 0.5 s of three items; convert frame indices to ms with source.fps; report the median offset per event.
evidence_required: frames: F8 at three item starts
questions.challenge: Check the fps used for conversion matches A7 stream r_frame_rate.

questions.question: What does the cut density look like across the video in 10-second windows?
questions.why_it_matters: Shows pacing shape (flat, peaks at items, burst in hook) for the compiler.
questions.how_to_answer: Count shot starts per 10 s window; list counts in order.
questions.challenge: The last window is usually partial; normalise it or mark it.

questions.question: Are there freeze frames or speed ramps, and where?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds time-manipulation effects to the motion list.
questions.how_to_answer: F5 full-frame difference near zero for more than 0.5 s inside moving footage indicates a freeze; frame steps (F8) show ramps.
questions.challenge: Stills with no Ken Burns also show zero difference; a freeze must follow moving footage in the same shot.

questions.question: Of 10 randomly sampled detected cuts, what share are real shot changes (shot-detector precision on this video)?
questions.why_it_matters: Calibrates trust in shot_stats for this video.
questions.how_to_answer: Pick 10 cuts at random from evidence.shots[]; inspect F8 at each and count real shot changes (not flashes, fast pans or text pops). Report the share and list the sampled cut times in the note; the challenger lowers pacing answers built on shot counts when it is below 0.9.
questions.challenge: Report which cuts were sampled so the check can be repeated.

questions.question: What is the ratio of text-change rate to cut rate?
questions.why_it_matters: Tells the compiler how many caption or label changes to schedule per shot.
questions.how_to_answer: Number of distinct on-screen text changes (from text_regions) per minute divided by cut_rate_per_min.
questions.challenge: text_regions are sampled; a change between samples may be missed. State the sampling interval.

questions.question: Does pacing differ between narrated stretches and stretches with no narration?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule for music-only segments.
questions.how_to_answer: Median shot length for shots mostly inside speech segments versus mostly outside.
questions.challenge: If narration covers more than 90% of the runtime, the second group is too small; say so.

questions.question: How long is the final shot?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the end hold.
questions.how_to_answer: Last element of evidence.shots[] duration_s.
questions.challenge: Check against the dead-tail answer in the structure lens.

questions.question: Is the median cut interval close to an integer multiple of the music beat period?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule to quantise shot lengths to beats.
questions.how_to_answer: Compute cut intervals modulo the beat period (60 / tempo_bpm); report the share within 15% of a beat of a multiple.
questions.challenge: Report the chance rate for the same tolerance (0.3 for 15% either side); a share near it is not evidence.

questions.question: What is the minimum time any text card stays on screen per word shown on it (ms per word)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets a readability floor for text holds.
questions.how_to_answer: For caption or label cards, divide on-screen duration (text_regions first to last t_s, or captions[] end_s - start_s) by word count; report min and median.
questions.challenge: Word-by-word highlighted captions keep the card while words change; use card duration, not word duration.
